[SP/FA] Octa 3 Monthly Test 2 Review Sheet
Reading · Unit 3 Lesson 1
About a hundred years ago, women's lives were very difficult. They were different from women's lives today.

In the 1890s, people thought women were not equal to men. Women had no right to vote. Also, most women couldn't go to college or have jobs. So they became full-time housewives. They looked after their children and did all the housework alone. Housework was really hard because they had to do it all by hand.

Women's lives have changed a lot. Today, people think women are equal to men. All women have the right to vote. Some women decide to be full-time housewives, but it's their choice. Many women go to college or have jobs now. Also, women use household appliances. These help women with housework.

How will women's lives change in another hundred years?
1. What is the purpose of the passage?
(A) to show how women's lives changed over time
(B) to show the easy lives of men and women
(C) to talk about women's choices
(D) to see how men are different today
2. What is true about women in the past?
(A) Many women could go to college.
(B) They went to work every day.
(C) Women did not have the right to vote.
(D) They shared the housework with their husbands.
3. How did women do housework in the 1890s?
(A) They used household appliances.
(B) Other people helped them.
(C) They did it with the men.
(D) They did it all by hand.
4. What does the writer think about household appliances?
(A) Women's lives are easier with them.
(B) They help women at work.
(C) It is cheap to buy them.
(D) Women need them to get jobs.
5. What does the underlined sentence mean?
(A) Some women choose to stay home full-time.
(B) Some women want to work for their family.
(C) Many women decide to work full-time.
(D) Women like to share the housework.

[SP/FA] Octa 3 Monthly Test 2 Review Sheet
Reading · Unit 3 Lesson 2
Maya sits with Nana and her mother. Nana is Maya's great-grandmother. They tell Maya stories about their lives. Maya thinks their lives are very different from one another.

Maya's great-grandmother grew up in the country. In her time, men and women were not equal. Only men could go to college and vote. Nana didn't go to college. Instead, she got married when she was 20 and became a full-time housewife. She did all the housework. Also, she raised 10 children and didn't earn money.

Maya's mother grew up in the city. She learned that men and women were equal. She went to college and got married at 35 years old. Both Maya's mother and father have jobs now. They share housework. Many household appliances help them. Her parents use these to save time.

Maya wonders what her life will be like when she grows up.

[SP/FA] Octa 3 Monthly Test 2 Review Sheet
Reading · Unit 4 Lesson 1
Rick was a security guard. He worked hard for everyone's safety at Morgan Stanley. The Morgan Stanley offices were in the World Trade Center in New York. In 1993, a terrorist group attacked the World Trade Center.

Rick thought he had to create an emergency plan. So he made one. He made all the workers practice it. Some people weren't happy. But Rick believed they needed practice.

On September 11, 2001, two planes hit the World Trade Center. Everyone at Morgan Stanley remembered the emergency plan. They met in the hallways. Then they walked down the stairs in pairs. The practice helped. Morgan Stanley lost only six of its 2,687 workers. Rick made sure everyone got out safely, and then he went back to help other people. Unfortunately, he lost his life.
1. Who is Rick?
(A) a doctor at the emergency center
(B) a security guard at Morgan Stanley
(C) a police officer in New York
(D) a builder for the World Trade Center
2. What happened at the World Trade Center in 1993?
(A) Rick's plan saved many people.
(B) 2,687 workers could not get out of the building.
(C) A group of terrorists got hurt in an emergency.
(D) A terrorist group attacked the World Trade Center.
3. How did workers feel about Rick's emergency plan at first?
(A) They wanted to practice more.
(B) Some people were not happy.
(C) All the workers liked the idea.
(D) They thought the plan was helpful.
4. In 2001, what did Rick do after all the Morgan Stanley workers got out?
(A) He made a new emergency plan.
(B) He went back to save others.
(C) He helped people in the hallway.
(D) He looked for the planes.
5. What might we know about Rick?
(A) He was a brave and strong person.
(B) He got hurt at work in 1993.
(C) He earned a lot of money from the plan.
(D) He did not like practicing an emergency plan.
